title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Window Over Which Lost Visits Are Counted
content:
## Service coordinator note

The visits counted as lost on a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record are read over a window that widens with the length of the withdrawal. A booking the office attended and closed as a no-access call is taken as answered and is never counted as lost.

The length of the withdrawal is the days from the day coverage was suspended to the day of the reading.

| Length of the withdrawal | Visits counted as lost |
|---|---|
| more than 60 days | those booked for a day in the last 6 months with no visit completed against them |
| more than 30 days but no more than 60 | those booked for a day in the last 3 months with no visit completed against them |
| no more than 30 days | the booked visits of the agreement with no visit completed against them |

### Boundary days

- At exactly 30 days withdrawn: "no more than 30", so every booked visit of the agreement with no visit completed against it is counted, with no window.
- At exactly 31 days: the window is the last 3 months.
- At exactly 60 days: still no more than 60, so the window is the last 3 months.
- At exactly 61 days: the window is the last 6 months.

### Worked case (hypothetical)

An agreement withdrawn for 75 days, with 5 visits booked for a day in the last 6 months and 2 visits completed in that span: 3 visits are counted as lost. Had the withdrawal run 40 days, the count would be taken over the last 3 months instead.
